peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is PVP in lab?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Abstract. Polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) is a water-soluble polymer obtained by polymerization of monomer N-vinylpyrrolidone. PVP is an inert, non-toxic, temperature-resistant, pH-stable, biocompatible, biodegradable polymer that helps to encapsulate and cater both hydrophilic and lipophilic drugs.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What type of polymer is PVP?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Polyvinylpyrolidone (PVP) is a linear nonionic polymer that is widely used in hair care formulations around the world. PVP polymers are considered the work-horse of the industry and have been prevalent for decades. PVP is an excellent film-former that forms stiff, transparent, shiny films.
